Article Title: Australia gamble on no warm-up games ahead of five-Test Border-Gavaskar Trophy 2027
Article Text:
Australia to skip practice matches ahead of 2027 BGT (Image: ICC)

No practice matches before India tour

Preparations to begin after New Zealand series

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Focus on replicating Indian conditions

Five-Test Border-Gavaskar Trophy begins in Nagpur

Test Date Venue 1st Test January 21-25 Vidarbha Cricket Association Stadium, Nagpur 2nd Test January 29-February 2 M. A. Chidambaram Stadium, Chennai 3rd Test February 11-15 Dr. Bhupen Hazarika Cricket Stadium, Guwahati 4th Test February 19-23 JSCA International Stadium Complex, Ranchi 5th Test February 27-March 3 Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad

Australia head coach Andrew McDonald has revealed that his side will not play any practice matches before the 2027 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India, opting instead for an extended training camp tailored to Indian conditions.The five-Test series, scheduled from January 21 to March 3, 2027, marks the first time the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India will be played over five matches after 57 years. The visitors have not won a Test series on Indian soil since the 2004-05 season.Speaking to cricket.com.au about Australia's preparations, McDonald said the team already has sufficient cricket before arriving in India, making traditional tour games unnecessary."We feel as though we've got enough time to immerse ourselves in those conditions. We won't be taking on a practice game. It'll just be more around the location. We've got a couple of options there. We have gone to the UAE previously and we have also gone into India last time into Bangalore, so we're just working through what that would look like in terms of how we then manage the individuals, " McDonald said.Before travelling to India, Australia will play a four-Test home series against New Zealand.McDonald indicated that the squad for India may differ from the one that finishes that series, with selection likely to be based on the specific demands of Indian conditions."A lot of that would happen on the back of the four Tests against New Zealand, seeing where players are at. We'll potentially have some different players with different skill sets that we believe can perform in India, so it won't necessarily be the squad that finishes the Test series (against NZ that then heads to India).There'll be some players that we need to put a little bit more prep into, and that'll start in Australia also, balancing out Big Bash commitments and things like that, " he added.McDonald stressed that Australia's priority is identifying a training base capable of replicating the pitches, weather and overall environment expected during the series opener."Ultimately, if you can have a dedicated venue that you're able to use and replicate as close to the conditions that you believe you may get in the first Test match or throughout a Test series, that's ideally what you want. You case those locations – you want a connection in terms of conditions and climate. We believe we'll get that right in terms of where we go, it just hasn't been confirmed yet, " Head Coach said.Australia have previously held pre-tour camps in the UAE and Bengaluru before touring India, and a similar strategy remains under consideration.
Article Summary: Australia will not play any practice matches before the 2027 Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India. The five-Test series, scheduled from January 21 to March 3, 2027, will be played over five matches after 57 years. Australia have not won a Test series on Indian soil since the 2004-05 season.

Article Title: Can Gambhir ace red-ball test in Sri Lanka?
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir (Image credit: ICC Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When Gautam Gambhir landed in Colombo with the Indian team on Tuesday, he did so carrying a contradiction that increasingly defines his tenure as India’s head coach. Few Indian cricketers have spoken more passionately about how sacred Test cricket is to them. Few modern Indian batters built their reputation on tougher overseas assignments quite like Gambhir did.He scored a marathon 137 in Napier to save a Test in New Zealand in 2009, made a century in Wellington and played one of the grittiest innings of his career in Cape Town in 2011 with a swollen hand, helping India secure a series draw in South Africa.Yet, two years into his coaching tenure, the format he values most has become his biggest Achilles heel. If Gambhir’s white-ball record has largely justified his appointment, his Test results have largely generated some very uncomfortable questions.More importantly, with India now staring at the prospect of missing a second consecutive World Test Championship (WTC) final under him, the two-Test series against Sri Lanka beginning on Aug 15 could become the most important assignment of his coaching career.The contrast between Gambhir’s fortunes across formats is striking.In white-ball cricket, his fingerprints are unmistakable. India won the 2025 Champions Trophy and followed it up with the 2026 T20 World Cup title. Gambhir pushed a philosophy built around relentless aggression rather than stat-padding and wicket-preservation.The approach reached its peak during India’s triumphant T20 World Cup campaign, when the team blasted 250-plus totals in both the semifinal and the final. As coach, he has consistently shown a preference for multi-skilled cricketers. In limited-overs cricket, where batting depth can often be the difference between victory and defeat, that approach has largely worked. In Tests, that approach has not worked.His preference for bowling allrounders and lower-order batting depth has sometimes come at the expense of specialists.The most cited example remains Kuldeep Yadav’s inconsistent and restricted role despite being one of India’s most potent wicket-taking options. The results have reflected the uncertainty. After beginning with a comfortable 2-0 series win over Bangladesh, India suffered a humiliating 3-0 whitewash at home against New Zealand. An even bigger blow followed when they lost the Border-Gavaskar Trophy 3-1 in Australia.There was some recovery in England, where a young Indian side under new captain Shubman Gill drew 2-2. But that goodwill quickly evaporated after a 2-0 home defeat to South Africa on turning pitches exposed India’s long-standing issues against quality spin. The timing couldn’t be worse. A second World Test Championship cycle threatens to slip away without India featuring in the final. For a nation that made the first two WTC finals and views itself as one of the format’s standard-bearers, that would represent a significant regression.Compounding the pressure is the perception that everyone around Gambhir has already paid a price for poor performances.Most of the support staff that began this journey with him are now gone. Assistant coaches Abhishek Nayar and Ryan ten Doeschate, along with fielding coach T Dilip, have all exited. The departures have created the impression that lieutenants have effectively served as scapegoats for India’s failures.If the coaching staff has already been reshaped, the obvious question becomes: how much longer can Gambhir remain insulated if results don’t improve? Officially, the BCCI continues to back him. Publicly, there has been no indication that a change is imminent. Yet Indian cricket rarely operates in a vacuum.Looming in the background is VVS Laxman , currently heading the BCCI’s Centre of Excellence. Laxman’s reputation within Indian cricket remains exceptional and his stock has only risen after India’s young side completed a 3-0 T20I sweep of Zimbabwe recently.Sources suggest that while Gambhir is not facing an immediate threat, a poor tour of Sri Lanka could significantly alter the conversation. There are, however, significant factors. A former cricketer close to Gambhir believes the criticism often ignores the reality of a team undergoing major transition. “You must understand that Gambhir’s job hasn’t been easy so far. This has been a team in transition,” the former cricketer said.Former India opener and UAE coach Lalchand Rajput feels the calls for drastic action are premature. “I still feel that as a coach, there will be ups and downs. You can’t be winning all the time. The Indian team is going through a rebuilding process. And when the team is going through it, you have to give more time to the players and the coach,” Rajput told TOI. “Greats like Rohit and Kohli have quit two formats, while India have a new T20 captain in Shreyas Iyer, and tried several new players in the T20 series in England,” Rajput further justified.Former India coach Sandeep Patil believes India’s problems run deeper than just the head coach. “The Sri Lanka tour is crucial for everyone, why only Gambhir? If Gambhir has failed to perform, so have the players. It is not right to pick on one guy,” Patil said. Patil was particularly critical of India’s preparation methods. “We were not able to play spinners and lost the home series against New Zealand because they came prepared. They practised on turning wickets. Whereas, our team was practising at the CoE on good tracks,” he said.
Article Summary: Gautam Gambhir's Test results have largely generated some very uncomfortable questions. India now staring at the prospect of missing a second consecutive World Test Championship (WTC) final under him. The two-Test series against Sri Lanka beginning on Aug 15 could become the most important assignment of his coaching career.

Article Title: Carlos Alcaraz withdraws from Cincinnati Open, US Open title defence in doubt
Article Text:
Carlos Alcaraz

Wrist injury continues to derail season

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US Open title defence under threat

Rankings take another hit

Carlos Alcaraz's troubled 2026 season has suffered another major setback after the Spaniard officially withdrew from the Cincinnati Open due to his lingering right wrist injury, casting fresh doubt over his chances of defending the US Open title later this month.The 23-year-old, who lifted the Cincinnati crown in 2025, confirmed on Tuesday (August 4) that he will not be fit in time for the ATP Masters 1000 event, which runs from August 11 to 23. His withdrawal means Alcaraz will forfeit the ranking points earned from last year's title and head into the North American Grand Slam swing without a single competitive hard-court match.Alcaraz has been sidelined since suffering a right wrist injury during the Barcelona Open in April. Although he has recently returned to practice, tournament director Bob Moran confirmed that the Spaniard has not progressed far enough in his rehabilitation to compete at the highest level. The injury has already forced Alcaraz to miss both the French Open and Wimbledon, an unprecedented absence from two consecutive Grand Slams during what should have been the prime phase of his career.The timing of the withdrawal could hardly be worse. With the US Open beginning on August 30, Alcaraz is now expected to enter Flushing Meadows without any competitive preparation on hard courts, assuming he is fit enough to participate.While he remains on the tournament's official entry list, the lack of match fitness raises serious questions about his ability to defend the title he won last year. Returning from a long injury layoff is challenging enough, but doing so at a Grand Slam without any tune-up events significantly increases the difficulty.The prolonged absence has also affected Alcaraz's position in the ATP rankings. Once firmly established among the tour's top two players, he has slipped to World No. 3, trailing both Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev.
Article Summary: Carlos Alcaraz has withdrawn from the Cincinnati Open due to a wrist injury. The withdrawal casts fresh doubt over the Spaniard's chances of defending the US Open title later this month. The 23-year-old has been sidelined since suffering a right wrist injury during the Barcelona Open in April.

Article Title: Para badminton champions left waiting as Rs 5 crore-plus cash awards remain pending
Article Text:
New Delhi, Jan 12 (IANS) India’s para-badminton Pramod Bhagat and Sukant Kadam

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Even as India basks in the glow of its successful Commonwealth Games campaign in Glasgow, several of the country’s top para badminton players, including Paralympic and world champions, are still waiting for cash awards promised by the sports ministry for achievements dating back to 2024.More than 20 players are awaiting payments worth several lakhs despite making repeated representations to the ministry and the Sports Authority of India (SAI).Figures accessed by TOI reveal that world No. 1 Sukant Kadam is yet to receive Rs 34.5 lakh, Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar Rs 31 lakh, former world champion Pramod Bhagat Rs 40 lakh and Paralympic gold medallist Krishna Nagar Rs 28 lakh.The unpaid rewards relate to medal-winning performances at the 2024 Para Badminton World Championships, 2025 Asian Para Badminton Championships and 2026 Para Badminton World Championships. The total outstanding payouts for the three events amount to Rs 1.87 crore, Rs 1.83 crore and Rs 1.42 crore respectively.The issue has now spilled into the public domain, with several para badminton players recently tagging Prime Minister Narendra Modi on social media, urging him to intervene and ensure the release of the pending cash awards.Warning that athletes could be forced to seek legal recourse, Nitesh Kumar questioned the rationale behind the delay.“The World Championships are premier sporting events and often serve as Olympic or Paralympic qualifiers. World Championships medallists in other sports have received cash awards in the past as well as in recent times. In fact, we were granted cash awards for our medals at the 2019 Para Badminton World Championships, which also served as a Paralympic qualifier, establishing a clear precedent for recognizing World Championship achievements,” Kumar said.Kadam, meanwhile, questioned why para badminton had effectively been left out under the revised cash award policy.“Medallists in other sports have received cash awards for these three championships, yet no para badminton medallist has been paid till now. We are only asking for parity and the implementation of the policy that has benefitted athletes in other disciplines,” Kadam said.
Article Summary: India’s top para badminton players are still waiting for cash awards promised by the sports ministry. More than 20 players are awaiting payments worth several lakhs. The unpaid rewards relate to medal-winning performances at the 2024 Para Badminton World Championships.

Article Title: Reality check after Commonwealth Games 2026: India’s boxing renaissance to face ultimate Asian exam
Article Text:
New Delhi, Aug 04 (ANI): Union Minister Kiren Rijiju in a group photograph with Indian boxing contingent (@KirenRijiju X/ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. After returning from Glasgow with a historic haul of seven gold and three silver medals, India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.The CWG triumph underlined the country’s growing depth, particularly in women’s boxing. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) struck gold, while Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg) topped the podium in the men’s competition. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal added silver medals.The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya, however, will be on an entirely different scale. Unlike the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will feature continental powerhouses such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan and North Korea — nations that have consistently dominated the World Championships and the Olympics.Uzbek stars Mirazizbek Mirzakhalilov and Bobo-Usmon Baturov, along with Kazakhstan’s Kairat Yeraliyev and Ablaikhan Zhussupov, are expected to headline a field packed with world-class talent.India will also be without two of its Commonwealth champions. Jaismine (57kg) and Arundhati (70kg) will miss out because their weight categories do not feature in the Asian Games programme, depriving the country of two genuine medal prospects.“The Asian Games for us is like the Olympics,” Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said. “The best teams in the world today are Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and India, and all three are in Asia. Add a strong Chinese contingent and you understand why it is much tougher. You can’t replicate this (CWG) performance at the Asian Games. But if you win a sizeable number of medals at the Asian Games, you can be hopeful of winning medals at the Olympics too.Women’s head coach Santiago Nieva shared a similar assessment while insisting the team remains on the right path.“We can’t guarantee that we will win gold all the time, but we are on the right track. We know how strong the field will be at the Asian Games. The boxers are aware that they can’t sit on their success,” he said.India had returned with one silver and three bronze medals from the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. The Glasgow CWG showcased the strides the boxing contingent has made. But it’ll be Aichi-Nagoya that is going to reveal whether the progress is enough to challenge Asia’s finest and signal genuine medal potential for the 2028 Olympics.
Article Summary: India's record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism. But the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.

Article Title: Rock, paper, scissors... then millionaire!: Australian Open brings back Million-Dollar 1 Point Slam
Article Text:
Australia's Jordan Smith holds his trophy aloft after defeating Joanna Garland of Taiwan to win the 1 Point Slam event ahead of the Australian Open in Melbourne, Australia, Jan. 14, 2026. (James Ross/AAP Image via AP, File)

From amateur to millionaire

One point decides everything

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tennis stars , amateurs and celebrities on one court

The Australian Open is bringing back one of its most talked-about innovations after confirming that the Million-Dollar 1 Point Slam will return during the tournament's Opening Week in 2027. Tournament organisers announced on Wednesday that the fan-favourite exhibition event will once again offer a staggering AUD 1 million (approximately USD 705,000) to the winner ahead of the year's first Grand Slam, which runs from January 17 to 31 at Melbourne Park.The announcement follows the overwhelming success of the inaugural edition, where an unknown local amateur stunned some of tennis' biggest names to walk away with a life-changing prize.The debut edition produced one of the most remarkable stories of the 2026 Australian Open. Local amateur Jordan Smith defied the odds by eliminating World No. 1 Jannik Sinner before going all the way to claim the AUD 1 million prize. Smith secured the title after Taiwan's Joanna Garland sent a two-handed backhand wide on just the third shot of the final point, instantly turning the Australian into a millionaire.Unlike conventional tennis tournaments, the 1 Point Slam is built entirely around sudden death.Every match consists of just one point. Before play begins, the two competitors decide the server through a game of rock, paper, scissors. The chosen server gets only one opportunity to put the ball in play. A fault, double fault or let that fails to land legally results in immediate elimination. Once the serve is in, the rally continues until the point is won, with the victor progressing to the next round. The knockout format creates constant jeopardy, ensuring every shot carries enormous significance.One of the biggest attractions of the event is its diverse field. The tournament features professional players, local amateurs and celebrities competing in the same draw. Last year's edition included Grand Slam champions Carlos Alcaraz, Iga Swiatek, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Alexander Zverev, while Taiwanese music superstar Jay Chou also took part.Chou's campaign ended almost instantly after he was knocked out by an ace from Petar Jovic without managing to hit a single ball, a moment that perfectly captured the drama and unpredictability of the format.
Article Summary: The Million-Dollar 1 Point Slam will return during the tournament's Opening Week in 2027. Tournament organisers announced on Wednesday that the fan-favourite exhibition event will once again offer a staggering AUD 1 million (approximately USD 705,000) to the winner. Last year's edition included Grand Slam champions Carlos Alcaraz, Iga Swiatek, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Alexander Zverev. Local amateur Jordan Smith defied the odds by eliminating World No. 1 Jannik Sinner.

Article Title: Military personnel bag 46% of India’s medals at CWG 2026
Article Text:
India's Jaismine Lamboria celebrates after winning the women's 57kg boxing final. (AP Photo)

NEW DELHI: Indian military personnel contributed the lion’s share in the country’s CWG medals tally. The Indian Army won 16 medals of India’s total haul of 39. Two Indian Navy personnel also won medals.If the medals won by Army and Navy personnel are combined, the services personnel bagged 18 medals out of the total 39, which is equivalent to 46% contribution of the services in winning medals.“A contingent of 20 Indian Army athletes won 16 medals”, the Army said, adding out of 16 medals, eight are gold, seven silver and one bronze.Praising its personnel, the Indian Army, in a post X on Monday, said, “Har kaam, desh ke naam. General Dhiraj Seth, COAS and All Ranks of Indian Army extend heartiest congratulations to the Indian Army athletes for their outstanding performance.”
Article Summary: The Indian Army won 16 medals of India’s total haul of 39. Two Indian Navy personnel also won medals. If the medals won by Army and Navy personnel are combined, the services personnel bagged 18 medals out of the total 39.

Article Title: Glasgow done, all eyes on 'Amdavad 2030': India's campaign offers both promise and warning signs
Article Text:
Indian boxer Jaismine Lamboria and other athletes during the closing ceremony of the CWG 2026. (PTI Photo)

Athletics leads the way



Boxers make a statement



Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Judokas earn their place in the spotlight



PUNE: The Glasgow Commonwealth Games are over. The baton passes to India for the Commonwealth Games in Ahmedabad, dubbed ‘Amdavad 2030’. With the event returning home after 20 years, India will be aiming not only to stage a better Games than Delhi 2010 but also to improve on its best-ever medal haul. At the 2010 Delhi Games, India won a record 101 medals to finish second in the overall standings.For Indian sport, Glasgow offered a mixed picture. The 39 medals collected this time were fewer than the 61 in Birmingham 2022, 66 in Gold Coast 2018 and 64 in Glasgow 2014. More importantly, those medals came from just six sports. By contrast, India’s medals had come from 17 sports in 2010, 11 in 2014, 15 in 2018 and 13 in 2022.The explanation lies partly in the programme itself. Glasgow did not include sports where India has traditionally been strong. India has won 135 medals in shooting between 1966 and 2018, excluding the 1970 Edinburgh edition. Wrestling has fetched India 114 medals across 18 editions since 1934. Yet Glasgow had no shooting, wrestling, hockey, badminton, archery or table tennis, which together had contributed 67 medals for India in Delhi 2010.As India prepares to host in 2030, the focus will be on retaining the positives from Glasgow while also bringing back its strongest disciplines.Athletics emerged as the biggest winner for India, with medals in the men’s 10,000m and 5,000m long jump, decathlon, high jump, triple jump and para-athletics adding up to 16 medals. What stood out most was the history made by Gulveer Singh, who won silver in the 10,000m and bronze in the 5,000m and Tejaswin Shankar, who claimed decathlon bronze.Yash Vir Singh also broke new ground by winning a javelin bronze in a field featuring Olympic and world champions, as well as world leaders and record holders. The para-athletes contributed three gold, two silver and one bronze, even as the 4x400m relay team had to settle for sixth place.“The performance was way better than expected. This has been a good result and it will only improve in the years to come. The result reflects the policies that the Athletics Federation of India (AFI) has adopted in the past few years,” former World Championships bronze medallist and current AFI senior vice-president Anju Bobby George told TOI.“Now we plan the training programme according to individual athletes’ requirements rather than designing a blanket programme for everyone. Some athletes train in the USA, some in Europe, because that is what best suits their future. The results are definitely going to improve in 2030 and beyond, as we also plan to host the Olympics,” she added.Boxing also delivered strongly, with seven gold among the 13 medals won. While the level of competition at the Commonwealth Games is not as demanding as at the Asian Games or Olympics, the performances will still provide a valuable confidence boost.“It is not as if these were the only medals our boxers have won so far. We had world champions, an Olympic medallist and Asian Games and Asian Championships winners at the Glasgow CWG. The field may not have been as strong as the Asiad, but it was not weak either.A good show at a competition like this gives a boost to the boxers,” 2008 Beijing Olympics bronze medallist Vijender Singh told TOI.With two historic gold and three medals overall, Indian judokas Asmita Dey, Harsh Singh and Yamini Mourya also deserve special mention. A sport that has often struggled for attention in the past appears to be finding its footing.If judo can continue on this trajectory, the possibilities are immense. With 15 medal events at the Olympics and proper investment and a cleaner administrative setup, India has genuine medal potential at the world level too.
Article Summary: Athletics emerged as the biggest winner for India, with medals in the men’s 10,000m and 5,000M long jump, decathlon, high jump, triple jump and para- athletics adding up to 16 medals. Boxing also delivered strongly, with seven gold among the 13 medals won. Judo also deserves special mention, with two historic gold and three medals overall.

Article Title: PCB appoint Michael Smith as batting coach ahead of England series on two-year deal
Article Text:
Michael Smith (Image: X)

Pakistan look to fix long-standing batting woes



Batting collapses continue to haunt Pakistan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Pakistan tour of England

Pakistan have officially appointed former South Africa first-class cricketer and coach Michael Smith as the batting coach of the men's national team, with the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) confirming the appointment on Tuesday.The 46-year-old has been handed a two-year contract and will oversee Pakistan's batting across both the red-ball and white-ball formats. Smith is set to begin his tenure ahead of Pakistan's three-match Test series against England, which starts on August 19.A Level 4 qualified coach, Smith enjoyed a decade-long playing career between 2003 and 2013, featuring in 89 first-class matches, 72 List A games and 16 T20s. He brings extensive coaching experience, having worked in the Pakistan Super League (PSL) with Islamabad United, Karachi Kings and Multan Sultans. His coaching résumé also includes stints as batting coach with Australia's Hobart Hurricanes and Cricket Tasmania, while he has also served as a coaching consultant for South Africa's KZN Inland and Eastern Province.Smith's appointment comes at a crucial time as Pakistan seek to address their recurring batting failures, particularly in pressure situations across formats. The national team has not had a full-time batting coach in recent times, with national selector Asad Shafiq occasionally stepping into the role.Meanwhile, former fast bowler Umar Gul continues as the team's bowling coach. Pakistan sit ninth in the ICC World Test Championship standings.Pakistan are currently touring the West Indies for a two-match Test series and are already trailing 0-1 after suffering a 90-run defeat in the opening Test. Despite being well placed at 244/3 in the first innings, they lost their final seven wickets for just 38 runs, before being bowled out for 120 while chasing 211 in the fourth innings.The second Test is already underway, and at stumps on Day 2, Pakistan were 76 runs behind with eight wickets in hand, still battling to level the series.Pakistan's fragile batting has become a recurring concern in recent years. Their inability to capitalise on strong positions has contributed significantly to a poor run in the longest format, with the team losing 13 of their last 17 Tests.The Pakistan men's cricket team is scheduled to tour England from August 19 to September 13, 2026, to play a three-match Test series. The matches form an integral part of the 2025–2027 ICC World Test Championship. Pakistan is currently concluding a red-ball tour in the West Indies and will arrive in England later this month, armed with newly appointed long-term batting coach Michael Smith to fix recent batting form issues.
Article Summary: Former South Africa first-class cricketer Michael Smith appointed batting coach. The 46-year-old has been handed a two-year contract and will oversee Pakistan's batting across both the red-ball and white-ball formats. Smith is set to begin his tenure ahead of Pakistan's three-match Test series against England, which starts on August 19. Pakistan are currently touring the West Indies and are already trailing 0-1.

Article Title: Wrestlers to challenge Brij Bhushan's acquittal; Vinesh, Bajrang say 'legal battle far from over'
Article Text:
Vinesh Phogat and Brij Bhushan Saran Singh (IANS Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Refusing to accept the trial court’s verdict, Vinesh Phogat on Monday said she and the other women wrestlers who accused former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexual harassment will challenge his acquittal before a higher court.Vinesh, who had publicly identified herself as one of the six complainants in the case, said the wrestlers have instructed their legal team to file an appeal at the earliest. Olympic medallist Bajrang Punia reiterated that their fight for justice would continue.Their decision came after additional chief judicial magistrate Ashwini Panwar of Delhi’s Rouse Avenue Court acquitted Brij Bhushan and former WFI assistant secretary Vinod Tomar in the 2023 sexual harassment case. According to the defence, the court found the evidence insufficient and noted inconsistencies and contradictions in witness testimonies before acquitting the two accused.Reacting to the verdict, Vinesh and Bajrang issued a joint statement on social media, saying the wrestlers’ legal battle was far from over.“We are deeply saddened that the court did not find Brij Bhushan guilty of the allegations of sexual harassment made by the women wrestlers.The women wrestlers have instructed their lawyers to appeal against this decision, and the appeal will be filed as soon as possible. We have not lost hope, and the wrestlers will continue their fight,” the statement said.The two also alleged that the complainants had faced sustained pressure throughout the case.“We had to gather a lot of courage to come out onto the streets and get an FIR registered against a powerful leader of the ruling party. Using his influence and political power, Brij Bhushan intimidated several girls into withdrawing their names. However, many women wrestlers stood firm and continued fighting against him in court,” they added.Vinesh had earlier chosen to publicly identify herself as one of the six women wrestlers who filed sexual harassment complaints against Brij Bhushan despite the anonymity generally maintained in such cases, citing the extraordinary circumstances surrounding the case and the pressure faced by the women wrestlers.The allegations against Brij Bhushan surfaced in 2023, triggering one of the biggest athlete-led protests in Indian sport. Vinesh, Bajrang, Rio Olympics bronze medallist Sakshi Malik and several other wrestlers staged a 36-day sit-in at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, demanding action against the then WFI chief over allegations of sexual harassment and intimidation. The protest eventually led to the Delhi Police registering an FIR and filing a chargesheet against Brij Bhushan under relevant IPC provisions. Tomar was also chargesheeted.In May 2024, the trial court framed charges against Brij Bhushan. Proceedings thereafter continued in camera, with final arguments concluding on July 2 this year. The court delivered its verdict on Monday, acquitting both Brij Bhushan and Tomar.Welcoming the judgment, Brij Bhushan said, “I said on the very first day that if the allegations are true, I will hang myself. I am very happy that I have been acquitted today. This is good news for me and my supporters.”He added, “This case has proved that even Olympians and Olympic medal winners can lie for their own interests. This is the victory of those players and supporters who had faith in me.”WFI presidentSanjay Singh also hailed the verdict. “On behalf of the Indian wrestling fraternity, we welcome this decision. These allegations caused significant damage to wrestling. This was politically motivated,” he said.Senior advocate Rebecca John, who represented four of the six complainants, described the acquittal as “deeply, deeply disturbing”. Speaking to PTI, she questioned claims made by the defence regarding the basis of the verdict, pointing out that the detailed judgment was yet to be made available. She added that the prosecution had argued any inconsistencies in witness testimonies which she cited were minor and did not undermine the credibility of the complainants.With the trial court proceedings now over, the case is set to move to the appellate stage, with the wrestlers expected to file their appeal before a higher court in the coming days.
Article Summary: Vinesh Phogat says she and other women wrestlers will challenge acquittal of Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. Olympic medallist Bajrang Punia reiterated that their fight for justice would continue. Vinesh had publicly identified herself as one of the six complainants in the case.

NEW DELHI: Pakistan moved closer to a rare away Test win after reducing West Indies to 103/6 at stumps on Day 3 of the second and final Test. Despite West Indies holding a lead of 60 runs, the hosts have only four wickets left, giving Pakistan the upper hand heading into the fourth day.West Indies ended the day on 103/6, leading by 60 runs with only four wickets remaining.Pakistan will look to dismiss the remaining batters quickly on Day 4 and chase a modest target to secure their first away Test victory since 2023. West Indies, meanwhile, are aiming to complete a 2-0 series sweep after winning the opening Test by 90 runs.Pakistan began the day still behind West Indies' first-innings total of 344, but Abdullah Shafique produced a superb unbeaten 160 to guide his team to 387.His innings helped Pakistan secure a 43-run first-innings lead before the visitors were bowled out.Left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican starred for West Indies with six wickets for 112 runs. He cleaned up the Pakistan lower order after already removing key batters earlier in the innings.Pakistan captain Babar Azam once again missed out on a Test century.He was run out for 88 after a brilliant direct hit from Brandon King ended his 183-run partnership with Shafique.Pakistan were still trailing by 63 runs when the wicket fell.Babar attempted a quick single after pushing the ball into the off side, but Shafique changed his mind and sent him back. King collected the ball and hit the stumps with a flat throw, leaving Babar short of his ground despite a desperate dive.It was Babar's highest Test score in 35 innings, but he is still waiting for his first Test century since scoring one against New Zealand in Karachi in December 2022.Brandon King's brilliant fielding effort came at a cost.The West Indies batter injured his lower back after landing awkwardly while throwing down the stumps. He had to be taken off the field, and it remains unclear whether he will be able to bat on Day 4.Warrican was the pick of the bowlers for West Indies.He dismissed debutant Awais Zafar for 1 before Shamar Joseph trapped Salman Ali Agha lbw. Warrican then bowled Mohammad Rizwan for 18 with the second new ball and later finished the innings by taking three wickets in four deliveries to complete a six-wicket haul.West Indies made a solid start to their second innings as Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Kavem Hodge added 40 runs for the opening wicket.However, Pakistan's spinners quickly took control.Sajid Khan removed Chanderpaul and Amir Jangoo before West Indies recovered through a partnership between Shai Hope and captain Roston Chase.The visitors then lost three wickets in the final five overs of the day. Sajid trapped Hope lbw for 15 and dismissed Jayden Seales for a two-ball duck. On the last ball of the day, Chase lost his concentration and chipped a simple return catch to Ali Usman after scoring 17.Sajid finished the day with figures of 4/32, while Usman picked up 2/29.

Article Title: ‘Catch-22 situation’: PCB challenges order to disclose confidential financial records

The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has approached the Islamabad High Court against orders asking it to share confidential financial information, players’ contracts and employee salary details.The Pakistan Information Commission (PIC) issued the directions under the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017, on July 9. The PCB has challenged the demand, arguing that making such information public could hurt its commercial interests and affect its negotiations.The commission has asked the PCB to provide its annual budgets for 2023-26, detailed spending records, players’ and employees’ contracts and salary information.It has also sought details of players and officials who travelled to this year’s T20 World Cup, the expenses involved and information about work carried out to upgrade Iqbal Stadium in Faisalabad.According to a report from news agency PTI, a PCB source described the situation as a "Catch-22 situation", saying that complying could encourage other institutions and committees to seek access to the board’s financial records, including information linked to theThe PCB has told the court that it operates in a highly competitive international sports environment and does not receive funding from the federal government or the Consolidated Fund, unlike government departments that depend on public money.The board argued that revealing private salary structures and contractual terms could damage its commercial interests and affect future contractual negotiations.It has also requested interim relief, warning that once personal financial and contractual information becomes public, any damage to its business interests, contractual relationships and the privacy of third parties could be impossible to reverse.
Article Summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has approached the Islamabad High Court against orders asking it to share confidential financial information. The Pakistan Information Commission (PIC) issued the directions under the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017, on July 9. The board argued that revealing private salary structures and contractual terms could damage its commercial interests and affect future contractual negotiations.

Article Title: 'Never got the credit he deserved': Sunil Gavaskar compares Ajinkya Rahane to Rahul Dravid
Article Text:
Ajinkya Rahane (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Batting great Sunil Gavaskar has paid tribute to former India captain Ajinkya Rahane , saying the veteran never received the recognition he deserved for his leadership despite guiding the team through one of the greatest triumphs in Indian Test history. Rahane , who announced his retirement from all forms of cricket last week, brought the curtain down on a distinguished career in which he often stepped up whenever the team needed him. While his contributions with the bat were significant, his captaincy during India's memorable 2020-21 Border-Gavaskar Trophy triumph in Australia remains one of the defining chapters of his career.India entered that series in turmoil after being bowled out for just 36 in Adelaide. Virat Kohli then returned home for the birth of his first child, while injuries ruled out several first-choice players as the tour progressed. Despite those setbacks, Rahane inspired India to a remarkable 2-1 series victory.Writing in his column for Mid-Day, Gavaskar compared Rahane's leadership to that of Rahul Dravid , saying both captains delivered outstanding results without receiving the appreciation they deserved.“His record as a skipper is exceptional, with four wins out of six and no losses. Like Rahul Dravid, who also had some terrific wins under his captaincy but never got the credit he deserved, so also Rahane’s leadership hardly got the applause that it merited,” Gavaskar wrote.He also criticised the tendency to overlook the captain's role when the team succeeds.“This is typical of Indian cricket. When the team wins, all praise goes to the individual achievers, be it batters and bowlers, but when the team loses, the captain and the coach get the blame,” he added.Gavaskar recalled how Rahane responded immediately after India's humiliating defeat in the opening Test of the Australia series by producing a match-winning century in Melbourne, setting the tone for an extraordinary comeback.“After the demoralising collapse of 36 all out in the first Test of the 2021 series Down Under, it was Rahane, along with Ravi Shastri, who picked the team from the dumps. The vice-captain took over a ship that was ready to sink and not only sailed it into calmer waters but also gave India an unprecedented first win at Australia’s fortress ‘The Gabba’ and with it the series victory too,” wrote Gavaskar.He also highlighted the significance of India's famous victory at The Gabba, achieved despite fielding an injury-ravaged side in the deciding Test.“In fact, in the final Test of the series, when most of the top players were unavailable due to injury, India pulled off one of its greatest victories in Test cricket. It proved once again, if ever it was needed, that nobody is indispensable in this game,” he added.Gavaskar concluded by praising Rahane's character, saying the former middle-order batter leaves the game with immense respect from teammates, opponents and cricket followers alike.“Rahane leaves the game with his head held high and the sincere thanks of cricket lovers for the totally selfless way he played the game. It’s not of many cricketers that it can be said that they did not have a single enemy in the game. There are perhaps less than a dozen to the best of my knowledge and experience. Ajinkya Rahane can take his place there with his typical humility,” Gavaskar concluded.
Article Summary: Rahane announced his retirement from all forms of cricket last week. His captaincy during India's Border-Gavaskar Trophy triumph in Australia remains one of the defining chapters of his career. India entered that series in turmoil after being bowled out for just 36 in Adelaide. Rahane inspired India to a remarkable 2-1 series victory.

Article Title: 'It's my fault': Ben Stokes blames himself for Brendon McCullum's England Test coach exit
Article Text:

Former England Test captain Ben Stokes has revealed that coaching the national side is his long-term ambition, while making it clear that his international playing career is over despite speculation about a possible return for the 2027 Ashes.Stokes called time on his England career following the recent Test series against New Zealand, ending a remarkable international journey. His retirement came after he missed the second Test of the series following an incident at a London nightclub.Speaking on thepodcast, hosted by Stuart Broad and Jos Buttler , Stokes said he is already preparing for life after retirement by working towards his Level Three coaching qualification."I know what I want to do in terms of staying within the game - which is to be a coach. I'm doing my level three coaching now while I'm still playing, because I want, when the day comes that I'm not playing any more, I'd love to be able to have all that stuff signed off and done," said Stokes.The 35-year-old admitted that taking charge of England in the future is a goal he hopes to achieve."I know what I want to do in terms of staying within the game, which is to be a coach.And would I love to be coach of England one day? Absolutely. I just really like the idea of being, again, like, in some form of leadership away from playing," he said.Stokes also spoke about England's decision to appoint Joe Root as Test captain after his retirement, revealing he had expected vice-captain Harry Brook to take over the role."I think just if you think someone's going to be a good captain or a good leader, then just give it to them. I understood the reasoning, but I was still like, well, what message is that sending to him?"He's vice-captain. And then the captain is not playing, but he's not captain. What?" said Stokes.Despite his surprise over the decision, Stokes backed Root to succeed in his second stint as skipper and praised new Test coach Stephen Fleming ."I love Rooty. I wish him nothing but success. I hope he goes on to achieve amazing things in his role of captain, and I think he's going to really enjoy it with Flem. He's a great man. I've worked with Flem before," he said.Stokes captained England's Test side from 2022 to 2026, partnering Brendon McCullum in a period that transformed England's approach to red-ball cricket through the aggressive style popularly known as 'Bazball'.McCullum stepped down from the Test coaching role two weeks after Stokes announced his retirement, with former New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming appointed as his successor. McCullum's four-year tenure began in 2022 and initially brought impressive results before England endured a difficult run, losing seven of their last nine Tests.Reflecting on McCullum's departure, Stokes jokingly blamed himself."I was surprised. If I hadn't made the decision that I made four weeks ago, Baz would still be coach. So it's my fault!" said Stokes.He also shared how he informed McCullum about his retirement."When I told Baz (about retirement), he was making toast, and I just went 'oh, I'm done'. I'd obviously had discussions with him anyway and then told him over toast."Then, again, he was like 'yeah, I've been given the tap on the shoulder' and I was like 'oh'. But he's still very excited and very happy to be moving forward with the white-ball because he's doing a very good job there."Stokes also dismissed suggestions that he could reverse his retirement and return for next summer's Ashes, despite England men's managing director Rob Key stating the door remained open."I never once thought, 'I'm just going to give it up and just keep going as a player'. I'm 35. If I'm not going to be captain, I think I'd find it tough to do it. Not saying because I'd find it tough to be led by someone else. I just think because I've given so much of this part of my career to my job, if I'm going to be play for England it's going to be as captain."I was very comfortable retiring from playing and not thinking about playing for England," he said.
Article Summary: Former England Test captain Ben Stokes has revealed that coaching the national side is his long-term ambition. Stokes made it clear that his international playing career is over despite speculation about a possible return for the 2027 Ashes. The 35-year-old admitted that taking charge of England in the future is a goal he hopes to achieve.

Article Title: 'India in a tough position': Ex-cricketer sounds WTC qualification warning ahead of Sri Lanka Tests

Former India opener Aakash Chopra believes India's chances of reaching the ICC World Test Championship (WTC) 2025-27 final hang heavily on the upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka, warning that the visitors are in a "tough position" in the race for the summit clash.India will begin their Sri Lanka tour with the opening Test on August 15. After nine matches in the current WTC cycle, India occupy fifth place in the standings with four wins and four defeats, giving them a points percentage (PCT) of 48.15.Sri Lanka, meanwhile, sit just below them in sixth place. They have registered one win, one loss and two draws so far, with a PCT of 41.67.Speaking on his YouTube channel, Chopra highlighted how significantly the standings could change depending on the outcome of the two-match series. He pointed out that a 2-0 defeat for India would dent their qualification hopes while boosting Sri Lanka's prospects."If we lose 2-0, we will remain at only 39 percentage points, and Sri Lanka will jump to 61 percentage points, and they will be No. 4. Sri Lanka will be in the run if they beat India 2-0. Then they have a realistic chance of going forward, or else it's a so-near-yet-so-far story for them," Chopra said.He added that a clean sweep would improve India's position, although not dramatically, while a drawn series would do little for either side."If we win this series 2-0, we will reach 57.58 percentage points. If we do a clean sweep, we will gain a little. If we draw the series 1-1, we won't gain anything because we will be at 48.48 and Sri Lanka will be at 44.44, and the positions will remain as is," he added.Chopra also underlined the difficulty of India's remaining WTC schedule. After the Sri Lanka series, India are set to travel to New Zealand for a two-Test series before hosting Australia in a five-Test contest early next year. According to Chopra, the shorter away assignments leave little room for error."Going forward, we have a two-match series in New Zealand, where it is difficult to win. Even if you lose one match, you lose 50 percentage points. It's going to be a tough one, and after that, there are five matches against Australia in India. India is in a tough position," Chopra added.India's upcoming assignments present a stern challenge. They have not won a Test series in New Zealand since the 2008-09 tour under MS Dhoni and have managed just two series victories there overall.The home series against Australia is also expected to test India after recent setbacks against SENA opposition. India were whitewashed by New Zealand and South Africa in successive home series, with the defeat to South Africa marking their first home Test series loss to the Proteas since 1999-2000. Under Temba Bavuma, South Africa also completed the rare feat of winning the ICC World Test Championship title and a Test series in India in the same year.India could also face a stiff examination in Sri Lanka, particularly against spin, an area that troubled them during their recent home series defeats to New Zealand and South Africa.
Article Summary: Former India opener Aakash Chopra believes India's chances of reaching the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 final hang heavily on the upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka. India will begin their Sri Lanka tour with the opening Test on August 15. After the Sri Lanka series, India are set to travel to New Zealand before hosting Australia in a five-Test contest early next year.

Article Title: 'Cricket has an alcohol culture, not just England': Ben Stokes opens up on drinking debate
Article Text:
Ben Stokes. (Reuters Photo)

'Cricket has a culture associated with alcohol'

Comments come after disciplinary controversy



Former England Test captain Ben Stokes has dismissed suggestions that England alone has a drinking problem, arguing that alcohol has long been embedded in cricket's culture across all levels of the sport.Speaking on the For The Love of Cricket podcast with former teammates Stuart Broad and Jos Buttler, the 35-year-old reflected on cricket's long-standing relationship with alcohol just weeks after announcing his retirement from international cricket.During the discussion, Broad put forward a question many fans have been asking in recent years: Does England cricket have a drinking problem? Stokes disagreed with the premise, insisting the issue extends far beyond one national team."No, I mean, that's such an extreme thing to put on a team. I think cricket has just a drinking culture and it hasn't changed. We are in 2026 now where the game has gone more professional over the years. One thing that has just stayed within cricket is its relationship with alcohol, from club cricket all the way up," Ben Stokes said.Stokes added that despite major advances in nutrition, medical support and athlete preparation, cricket's traditional association with alcohol continues to exist."It's been embedded within the sport. The relationship between alcohol and cricket is something that hasn't moved on as the game has become more professional. There's been more science, medicine and nutrition information. So people think England cricket has a culture with alcohol, but I would say no, cricket has a culture associated with alcohol, " he added.Stokes' remarks come against the backdrop of a recent disciplinary incident that saw him suspended for one Test after breaching team curfew during England's series against New Zealand.The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) stood down both Stokes and teammate Gus Atkinson for the second Test following a late-night outing. Although an investigation later cleared both players of further wrongdoing and they returned for the third Test, the incident prompted the ECB to introduce stricter alcohol guidelines for England players.Shortly after returning to the squad, Stokes announced his retirement from international cricket, bringing an end to his distinguished England career while continuing to pursue domestic and franchise cricket opportunities.
Article Summary: Former England Test captain Ben Stokes has dismissed suggestions that England cricket has a drinking problem. The 35-year-old argued that alcohol has long been embedded in cricket's culture across all levels of the sport. Stokes' remarks come against the backdrop of a recent disciplinary incident that saw him suspended.

Consistency is often the hardest quality to master in domestic cricket. Smaran Ravichandran has done exactly that. With 1534 runs in 26 innings at an average of 73.60, including three double hundreds in the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, the Karnataka batter has firmly established himself as one of the brightest young talents in the country and has shown that he is far from a one-season wonder.More importantly, Smaran has shown the versatility to excel across formats, seamlessly adapting his tempo to the demands of the game. He was the driving force behind Karnataka's 2024-25 Vijay Hazare Trophy triumph, ending the state's five-year wait for a major title. Smaran piled up 433 runs in seven innings at an average of 72.16, including two centuries and two fifties. In the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, he finished as Karnataka's leading run-scorer with 319 runs in seven innings, averaging 63.80 at a strike rate of 160.With back-to-back stellar seasons behind him, Smaran now has his sights set on the next step. In an exclusive conversation with TimesofIndia.com, the left-hander speaks about his India dream, the disappointment of missing out on the latest India A squad, his leadership ambitions, the art of succeeding across formats, and why his mother still refuses to let him ignore the value of education.ExcerptsI'm 100% fit now. The recovery has gone really well and I'm ready to play again.Missing the Emerging Teams tournament was heartbreaking because every opportunity matters. But there are plenty of things to look forward to this season. Right now, I'm fully fit and excited to get back on the field.Preparation becomes extremely important, especially during the off-season. A lot of credit goes to Syed (Zabiulla) Sir because he plans my training in a way that simulates the challenges I'll face during the Ranji Trophy. We train on different kinds of wickets, including red-soil and black-soil surfaces, and we deliberately practise on difficult pitches. Batting on flat wickets is comparatively easier because most batters can adjust, but scoring on challenging wickets requires a different level of preparation.In India, wickets tend to assist spin as the game progresses into the third and fourth days. So batting on those surfaces during practice is very important. It prepares you not only for the first innings but also for the second innings when conditions become tougher. Batting against different bowlers in different conditions has helped me overcome many challenges that come during matches.At times, he is very demanding, especially when it comes to discipline and following the process. He believes in completing every small task because those little things help you grow both as a cricketer and as a person.From my childhood, discipline and commitment to the game have always come first. As I grew older, he eased up a little, but his core values haven't changed. He still ensures that every practice session has purpose and quality because that's what ultimately helps you improve.Again, it comes back to off-season preparation. During training, I constantly switch formats. For example, I might spend two days batting with the red ball and then move straight to white-ball practice. Doing this repeatedly over four to six weeks helps your muscle memory and instincts adapt naturally.Switching from red-ball to white-ball cricket is comparatively easier because you're adding more scoring options. But moving back from white-ball to red-ball cricket can be challenging because you have to leave more deliveries and be patient outside off stump. I feel the off-season training helps my body and mind make those transitions smoothly.Not really. For me, it's more about mindset than technique. The red ball swings for longer and demands greater patience. You have to respect good spells and understand that you're batting for long periods to build an innings. As long as I'm in the right headspace and understand the match situation, I don't feel the need to change my technique.I definitely think it's possible. Playing in the V can still be effective, but you also need to develop a wider range of shots because bowlers constantly vary their pace and lengths in T20 cricket.It doesn't necessarily mean playing scoops or other unconventional shots, but you need enough options to make the bowler uncomfortable and force him to bowl where you want him to. Nowadays, teams are scoring and chasing 240 or even 250. To contribute consistently in that environment, you have to broaden your scoring areas while continuing to trust your natural strengths.Playing spin becomes increasingly important as you move up the levels, especially in the subcontinent, where pitches often assist spin more than seam. I feel the sweep and reverse sweep are very important because they force the spinner to change his lengths and lines.You can always rely on your defence, but if you want to score consistently and dominate quality spin bowling, you need those additional options.That's something I'm working on this season. Even if I don't use those shots on every wicket, it's important to have them in my game for turning tracks.Sunrisers Hyderabad have been fantastic as a franchise. They've always backed their players and created a very supportive environment. Sharing a dressing room with players like Ishan Kishan, Abhishek Sharma, Heinrich Klaasen and Travis Head was a huge learning experience. Watching how they prepare, practise and approach T20 cricket teaches you a lot.Coming into the IPL, I had scored plenty of runs in domestic cricket and I was confident. But that's the nature of the game. You don't score runs everywhere you go. It was a valuable learning experience. Last year I couldn't play because of the injury, so I was grateful to get six matches this season.Things didn't go according to plan, but I now know the areas I need to improve. The off-season gives me an opportunity to work on those aspects so that I'm better prepared for the next IPL and can contribute much more to the team.Definitely. I've always enjoyed leading teams. It's a privilege, and there's no better feeling than winning a championship as captain.I've captained Karnataka at the age-group level and we won the CK Nayudu Trophy. More recently, I was part of the Maharaja Trophy-winning side as well. Leadership is something I've always looked forward to, so if that opportunity comes, it would be a great honour.I knew the series was coming and naturally I was hoping to be part of the squad.Of course, I felt I had a chance, but I didn't dwell on it for too long. My focus immediately shifted towards scoring even more runs this season.Every year there's a different leading run-scorer in the Ranji Trophy. My goal is to remain at the top and continue piling on runs. Ultimately, your bat has to do the talking. India has so many quality cricketers that the only thing within your control is your performance. If I keep scoring consistently, opportunities will eventually come.Yes, ideally I would. I've always batted at No. 4. Last season, Karun Nair was batting there and both of us were scoring runs, so we didn't want to disturb a combination that was working well. If the opportunity comes, I'd love to bat in the top four. Whether that's No. 3 or No. 4 doesn't really matter.At the same time, my priority is helping Karnataka win championships. If batting at No. 5 gives the team the best chance of winning, I'm happy to do that as well.Sachin Tendulkar has been an inspiration to every cricketer growing up, but my number isn't because of him. I used to wear No. 5. One day my mother suggested that I switch to No. 10. I did, and I've never changed it since.My family has been incredibly supportive throughout my life.It was actually my mother who enrolled me in cricket coaching because I was a very naughty child. Syed Sir happened to coach at the ground near our home, and that's where everything started. My family comes from an academic background. Most of them are engineers, so cricket was something completely new for them. Even then, they never pressured me.The emphasis was always on balancing studies and cricket. My mother always ensured I did well in school and college while pursuing cricket seriously.Whenever I come home, they support me regardless of whether I've scored runs or not. My mother may ask what went wrong after a poor innings, but that's simply a mother's concern.Syed Sir has also been like family. He wasn't just my coach; he played a big role in convincing my parents to let me pursue cricket seriously. I also have an elder sister, who is six years older than me. She doesn't follow cricket closely but she always watches my IPL matches and sends me a message whenever I do well.I'm fortunate to have such a supportive family around me.(Laughs) Yes, absolutely. That's probably the conversation we have the most. She always reminds me that I should have a good educational background and a career beyond cricket.She believes studies are just as important, and I completely respect her viewpoint. Even today, I feel education and cricket should go hand-in-hand because balancing both teaches you a lot about discipline and life. Credit goes entirely to my family for helping me maintain that balance.
Article Summary: Smaran Ravichandran has delivered back-to-back outstanding Ranji Trophy seasons. He was the driving force behind Karnataka's 2024-25 Vijay Hazare Trophy triumph. Smaran has shown the versatility to excel across formats.

Article Title: Pakistan boxer Qudratullah ‘goes missing’ in Glasgow after Commonwealth Games campaign
Article Text:
Pakistan boxer Qudratullah

Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow, just hours before the country’s Commonwealth Games contingent was scheduled to leave for home.According to a report by Pakistani outlet Geo News, sources in the Pakistan Boxing Federation said Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. Officials later checked his room and found that he was no longer there.The Pakistan team was due to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before leaving for Pakistan. However, Qudratullah could not be found when officials checked his room, sources said.His passport and return ticket are reportedly still with the team manager. The incident is not the first such case involving a Pakistani boxer abroad, with another promising boxer, Zohaib, reportedly going missing during an international tour of Italy last year.Pakistan’s 21-member contingent finished the 2026 Commonwealth Games with only one medal. Boxer Fatima Zahra won bronze in the women’s 60kg category, giving Pakistan its only podium finish at the Games.The result was Pakistan’s lowest medal tally since the 1998 Commonwealth Games, when the country won one silver. Pakistan had also returned without a medal from the 1990 edition, making Glasgow its poorest CWG campaign in 36 years.Fatima made history by becoming the first Pakistani female boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal and was later chosen to carry the national flag at the closing ceremony.Pakistan’s biggest medal hope, Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem, also failed to finish on the podium after serving as the country’s flagbearer at the opening ceremony.
Article Summary: Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. Pakistan team was due to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before leaving for Pakistan. Pakistan’s 21-member contingent finished the 2026 Commonwealth Games with only one medal.

Article Title: ‘Like preparing for IIT and UPSC together’: Father Murali shares Sreeshankar’s comeback story
Article Text:
Murali Sreeshankar

KOCHI: S Murali gave an unusual analogy to describe the struggles his son, long jumper Sreeshankar Murali, undertook to regain full fitness after a career-threatening knee injury he sustained two years ago.“Sreeshankar’s comeback was as difficult as preparing for the IIT and Civil Services simultaneously,” he told TOI.Murali is currently near Prague, where he is closely monitoring his son’s training ahead of a busy stretch that begins with the World Athletics Continental Tour (silver level) meet in Bhubaneswar on Aug 22, followed by next month’s Asian Games in Japan.“Sreeshankar’s training now revolves around strength and conditioning, along with the prehab and rehab programme designed by coach Wayne Lombard. There is very little time to work on technique. The priority is to protect the knee on his take-off leg,” Murali said.His IIT-UPSC analogy aptly captures the magnitude of the challenge Sreeshankar faced after suffering the devastating injury just months before the 2024 Paris Olympics.Two years later, the journey came full circle when the 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.“Of all the medals Sreeshankar has won, this one gives me the greatest satisfaction because of the circumstances under which he achieved it. It reflects his mental toughness and hunger,” Murali said.The conditions in Glasgow were anything but favourable.“It was around 12 degrees Celsius with drizzle and strong winds, making the runway tricky,” Murali said. Despite the difficult conditions, Sreeshankar produced a best jump of 8.09m to finish second.The performance inevitably brought back painful memories of 2024, when the family received a grim diagnosis after Sreeshankar tore the patellar tendon in his take-off leg.“The doctors in Mumbai had not seen an injury like this. I thought he would never be able to walk again,” Murali recalled.“They told us it wasn’t a common sports injury but the kind usually seen after a serious car accident. His knee was completely ruptured.”Determined to find the best treatment, Murali travelled nearly 1,900 miles with his son to Doha’s Aspetar Hospital. “The surgeons reconstructed his knee using four screws.”The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process.The painstaking recovery paid rich dividends. Since returning to elite competition, Sreeshankar has consistently cleared the eight-metre mark, including a season’s best of 8.38m at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar in June.“There is no time to bask in the Commonwealth Games glory,” Murali said, pointing to the demanding schedule ahead.Sreeshankar will now turn his attention to the Asian Games in Japan, where he hopes to upgrade the silver medal he won at the previous edition in Hangzhou.“With everything Sreeshankar has gone through, he has every reason to believe he can stand on top of the podium at the Asian Games,” Murali concluded.
Article Summary: Sreeshankar Murali suffered a career-threatening knee injury two years ago. The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process. The 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week's Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: 'You are still a role model': CWG medallist Tejaswin Shankar hails Vinesh Phogat, recalls 2018 memories

Commonwealth Games 2026 bronze medallist Tejaswin Shankar has expressed his gratitude to star wrestler Vinesh Phogat for her words of encouragement after a knee injury forced him to withdraw from the high jump event at the recent Commonwealth Games.Shankar, a two-time Commonwealth Games medallist, was forced out of the high jump after his long-standing knee problem flared up during his opening attempt. The setback left the athlete devastated, with Shankar breaking down in tears after being unable to continue.Despite the disappointment, he bounced back strongly in the gruelling two-day decathlon, finishing with 7,976 points and securing his second Commonwealth Games medal. His national record in the decathlon stands at 8,057 points.Shankar has been dealing with chronic patellar tendinitis, commonly known as jumper’s knee.Following his withdrawal, Vinesh had reached out to him with a motivational message, urging him to remain focused and prepared for whatever came next.“Teju, you still can do it. Stay focused on what is ahead," Vinesh wrote on X. "My coach always said, as professional athletes, we must always be prepared for the best and at the same time, be ready for the worst.In life, everything happened for a reason, I guess. Rooting for you as always."Remembering Vinesh’s support, Shankar thanked her publicly and recalled how she had helped him feel comfortable during his first Commonwealth Games in 2018.Remembering her support, Shankar replied, “Thank you, Vinesh ji for your motivating words. I remember my first CWG in 2018 as a teenager when you made me feel comfortable and told me that I belonged there. 8 years later, you are still a role model."Meanwhile, Vinesh said the women wrestlers who accused former Wrestling Federation of India chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh of sexual harassment will appeal a Delhi court’s decision to acquit him.A Delhi court on Monday acquitted Brij Bhushan and co-accused Vinod Tomar in the sexual harassment case filed by the women wrestlers.
